text:
maya: Quick heads-up — quantized candidate reranker (ptq-v2) shows +0.8% NDCG@10 on holdout A but MRR dropped ~3% on the head query slice. Any immediate hypotheses?

sam: Repro link: http://ci.internal/runs/1769991234 — looks like the improvement is concentrated on long-doc queries. Curious about tokenizer/truncation differences.

maya: Eval command used: `python eval/run_rerank.py --model rerank-ptq-v2 --split holdoutA --batch 256 --seed 42`

lee: Can you paste a tiny diff sample (top wins/losses)? Short snippets are fine.

maya: pasted 5 example diffs:
```
Q: "migrate db schema"
old: doc42 label=1 score=1.24
new: doc42 label=1 score=0.47
old top: [42,7,12]
new top: [7,12,42]
```

eva: From a quick look that smells like either truncation/padding or a scoring calibration change — long docs get a boost, short high-precision answers can slide down.

sam: Did tokenizer config change when we exported the PTQ? Maybe special token ids or pad/truncation defaults flipped.

maya: Export snippet I used: `tokenizer.save_pretrained(...)` then `export_model(..., quantize=True)`. Config in repo: `tokenizer.pad_to_max_length=False, truncation=True` and we use left-truncation for docs.

lee: Left-truncation could push final answer tokens out for short queries when paired with different max_len handling. Try `--truncate_from right` as an ablation.

eval-bot: CI: rerank-eval job queued (1769991250) — tests: baseline vs ptq-v2 vs ptq-v2+trunc-right.

sam: Also check whether the candidate ordering changed during candidate dump. If doc IDs got shuffled the labels->positions mapping could be off.

maya: Verified candidate ids preserved in the sample; labels align. The per-query loss seems real. Example query "how to migrate db" shows short gold snippet outranked by long background pages in new model.

eva: Another possibility: previous float model applied an implicit rescale (we used to multiply logits by ~1.15 before softmax in some pipelines). Quantized export may have baked a different scale or removed it.

maya: Code currently: `scores = model(batch).squeeze() * 1.0` — looks like we rely on checkpoint having the right scale baked in. I'll diff checkpoints for any baked scaling factors.

lee: For quick signal, run 3 controlled ablations: 1) old tokenizer + ptq-v2, 2) ptq-v2 + right-truncation, 3) ptq-v2 with manual logit scale 1.15. Keep eval set small (200 head queries) to iterate fast.

sam: I'll queue those — ETA ~45-75m depending on queue. I created jobs: `eval/ablation/head200/baseline`, `.../ptq-origtok`, `.../ptq-trunc-right`, `.../ptq-scale-1.15`.

maya: Thanks. I'm also going to run a quick tokenization comparison on a handful of queries to check token counts and whether special tokens differ between exports: `python scripts/token_check.py --queries head200.txt --models float-v1,ptq-v2`

eva: Great. If it is tokenizer, the fix is simple (keep float tokenizer at export or normalize tokenization at eval). If it's scoring, we need the scale patch. Either way we should add a short note to the rerank-evals doc after we confirm. :thumbsup: 

maya: Will update this thread with results. For transparency I logged the initial run artifacts to `gs://redwood-evals/rerank/1769991234/`

sam: pinging when jobs finish, will post small CSV with NDCG/MRR deltas by slice.

maya: Appreciate it — if MRR stays down after ablations we might consider rolling back ptq-v2 for production.

eva: Agreed. Keep it small-run first.

maya: updating — starting ablations now, will report back in thread.
